entity_resolution.arabic_name: أبو علي، الحسن بن الحسن بن الهيثم

timeline_a_biological.event: Feigned madness to avoid punishment by Fatimid Caliph Al-Hakim after assessing Nile damming as unfeasible; placed under house arrest in Cairo.
Released from house arrest following the death of Caliph Al-Hakim; established residence near the Al-Azhar Mosque.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Began systematic experiments on camera obscura and light propagation while confined under house arrest.
Completed Kitab al-Manazir (Book of Optics), revolutionizing the study of light, refraction, reflection, and human vision.
Authored Al-Shukuk 'ala Batlamyus (Doubts Concerning Ptolemy), critiquing Ptolemaic planetary models on physical and logical grounds.
Posed and solved Alhazen's Problem regarding geometric reflections from spherical mirrors using conic sections.

physics_analysis.contribution_name: Intromission Theory of Vision and Camera Obscura Optics
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Resolving conflict between emission theory (light rays exit the eye) and classic intromission theory, while establishing rectilinear propagation of light.
physics_analysis.hypothesis: Vision occurs when light rays emitted or reflected from physical objects enter the eye in straight lines, forming a point-to-point representation.
physics_analysis.model_or_framework: Experimental geometric optics utilizing dark chambers (camera obscura) and mechanical aperture control.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Constructed controlled dark chambers with variable apertures to observe light rays passing through small openings, proving that rays travel in straight lines and do not mix at the aperture point.

variables_definition.h_o: Height of light source or object
variables_definition.d_i: Distance from aperture to image screen

equations.assumptions: Aperture diameter is small relative to focal distances; light travels strictly in straight lines without significant wave diffraction.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Disproved the ancient visual ray emission hypothesis; introduced controlled empirical experimentation and physical verification into optics.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Did not account for light diffraction or chromatic dispersion effects.

physics_analysis.contribution_name: Mathematical Catoptrics and Alhazen's Reflection Problem
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Finding the point on a spherical, cylindrical, or parabolic mirror at which a ray from a fixed light source reflects to a fixed observer.
physics_analysis.hypothesis: Reflection obeys the equal angle law with respect to the normal vector at the point of incidence, within a single plane of incidence.
physics_analysis.model_or_framework: Geometric catoptrics combining circle geometry and conic section intersections.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Utilized custom graduated iron instruments, tubes, and polished curved mirrors (spherical, cylindrical, parabolic) to measure angles of incidence and reflection empirically.

variables_definition.\\theta_i: Angle between incident ray and surface normal
variables_definition.\\theta_r: Angle between reflected ray and surface normal

equations.validity_domain: Specular reflection on smooth curved or flat surfaces
equations.assumptions: Surface is macroscopically smooth and polished; media boundary is isotropic.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Solved a fourth-degree polynomial geometry problem using conic sections; provided foundational principles used centuries later by Kepler, Huygens, and Snell.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Applies strictly to specular mirrors; geometric construction requires Euclidean/conic solution methods.

teachers: Ibn Sahl (intellectual influence in refraction geometry)
